header.name: Analytic foundations for elliptic curves and modular forms
header.description: This course develops the analytic background necessary for the study of modular forms and elliptic curves. Beginning with a review of holomorphic and meromorphic functions, Cauchy’s theorem, and residue calculus, the course proceeds to conformal mappings and Möbius transformations that describe the automorphisms of the unit disc and the upper half-plane. Students then explore the geometric structure of the upper half-plane and its quotient spaces, leading naturally to periodic and doubly periodic functions. The latter part of the course introduces the theory of lattices, the construction and properties of the Weierstrass ℘-function, and its connection to elliptic functions and elliptic curves, culminating in the analytic dependence on the modular parameter.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to demonstrate understanding of the theory of holomorphic and meromorphic functions, including Cauchy’s theorem, its consequences, and residue calculus.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply conformal mappings and Möbius transformations to describe automorphisms of classical domains and understand the geometry of the upper half-plane and its quotient spaces.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will develop knowledge on the periodic and doubly periodic functions and be able to construct lattices as a framework for defining elliptic functions.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to define the Weierstrass ℘-function, establish its key properties, and interpret elliptic functions and elliptic curves in terms of complex analysis and modular parameters.

lecture_topics: Möbius transformation: Definition, Properties and its fixed points
Automorphism of disc and upper half plane
Geometry of upper half plane and quotient spaces
